dev-v2-ext · Case 2836

Route deviation

My usual route is 11.5 km and the app says the matched route is 16.0 km, but we drove 16.96 km picking up someone else.

Ruling

No change NO_ACTION

No money moves. The charge stands.

The judge's explanation, as written

Both of you have been heard, and on this record the rider and the driver end up agreeing, and the evidence supports that agreement. This was a pooled ride (Ryde Pool, trip TRP-02836). Under the route-deviation policy the comparator for a pooled trip is the matched-itinerary distance the platform computed at match time. The trip record stores that as trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km (EV-TRIP-02836), and the platform's own source note describes it as a 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'. The rider's usual route of 11.5 km is carried separately as trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km and is reference only: POL-RD-12 says a claim measured against the solo figure has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. I name both figures (16.0 km matched, 11.5 km solo) so the rider can see why the 11.5 km comparison cannot be the baseline. The distance actually driven is taken from the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 16.96 km (EV-GPS-02836) govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km = 17.0 km. The excess is therefore 16.96 - 16.0 = 0.96 km, which is 6.00% of 16.0 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear BOTH 0.8 km absolute AND 20% of the optimal distance (3.2 km here), and both tests must pass. The 0.96 km clears the absolute limb, but 6.00% is far short of 20%. No route deviation is established. The rider's point that extra distance was driven picking up the co-rider does not change this. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess altogether, and the 16.0 km matched itinerary already includes that pickup, so there is no deviation for it to enlarge. Because no deviation is established, the POL-RD-02 fare recomputation is never reached. The only refund that survives a failed POL-RD-01 test is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and there is none here: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02836) carries no ERP gantry lines, tolls of SGD 0.00 and an airport surcharge of SGD 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge. The charged total of SGD 23.51 stands as billed. Two further points on the driver's account. First, the trace is clean: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and there is no data-failure escalation under POL-RD-10(3). Second, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02836-01 is missing from the bundle (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). No party relied on it as an exculpatory ground - the driver's answer is that the trip was pooled, not that traffic forced a detour - so POL-RD-03 was never invoked against it and its absence neither escalates the case under POL-RD-10(5) nor engages POL-RD-13. On the driver's record: POL-RD-01 records no material deviation, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 173 completed trips in 90 days (ratio 0.006), below both the 3-flag and the 0.05 thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral arises. The deciding measurements are carried by EV-GPS-02836 and EV-TRIP-02836, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is 0.90. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence, the charge of SGD 23.51 remains in place and no money moves (the monetary effect is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold). This ruling was made without human review and either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.
